references.text: The Ten Commandments give the fundamental law concerning the Sabbath: to remember the Sabbath day and keep it holy, and that the Lord blessed the Sabbath day.
Six days you shall do your work, but on the seventh day you shall rest - the same pattern of six working days and rest on the seventh.
The Sabbath is described as a holy day of rest for the Lord, where work is forbidden.
Six days shall work be done, but the seventh day shall be holy to you, a Sabbath of complete rest for the Lord.
Repetition of the Sabbath commandment in Deuteronomy, with the instruction to keep the Sabbath day holy.
The creation account where God rested on the seventh day and sanctified it - the theological foundation for the Sabbath.
Jeremiah exhorts the people not to carry burdens on the Sabbath day, but to keep it holy.
Jesus teaches about the Sabbath and declares that the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.
Jesus says that the Sabbath was made for man's sake, not man for the Sabbath's sake.
Discussion about healing on the Sabbath and the true purpose of the Sabbath.
There remains a Sabbath rest for the people of God - the spiritual fulfillment of the Sabbath rest.
